name: Refugio-Museo de la Guerra Civil, Cartagena
story: Cartagena was the Republic's main naval base and home of its fleet, which made it one of the most heavily bombed cities of the war. After a four-hour raid by the Condor Legion on 25 November 1936, the city began tunnelling shelters into its hills. This gallery, cut into the Cerro de la Concepción, was designed for more than 5,000 people and was still unfinished when Cartagena fell on 31 March 1939. Estimates of the number of raids the city suffered vary widely, from about 40 to 117. Opened as a museum in 2004, it covers daily life under the bombs, passive and active air defence (DECA), and the damage to the city. It is the best introduction to the war in the south-east.
see: A long tunnel in the hillside with exhibition rooms, photographs, air-raid sirens and audiovisuals; a panoramic lift beside it rises 45 m to the Castillo de la Concepción.
plan: Run by Cartagena Puerto de Culturas; entry is paid, and a combined ticket with other city museums is available. Entrance is on Calle Gisbert, in the centre, a 10-minute walk from the port.
